title: Conjecture 7
statement_text: We have that $T(n) = \widetilde{\Theta}(\sqrt{n})$. More generally, we have that $T(G) = \widetilde{\Theta}(\sqrt{|G|})$.
context_text: All groups are abelian. For subsets $W,C$ of a group $G$, $C$ is a complement for $W$ if $W+C=G$, and a minimal complement for $W$ if moreover no proper subset of $C$ is a complement for $W$; $C$ is a minimal complement in $G$ if it is a minimal complement for some $W\subseteq G$. For a finite abelian group $G$, $T(G)$ is the greatest $T$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at most $T$ is a minimal complement in $G$, and $T(n)$ is the minimum of $T(G)$ over abelian groups of order $n$. The authors prove $T(n)\ge\frac{n^{1/3}}{2(\log n/\log2)^{2/3}}$ (every non-empty $C$ with $|C|\le2^{2/3}n^{1/3}/(3e\log n)^{2/3}$ is a minimal complement), $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T(n)/\sqrt{n}\le\sqrt2$ (using groups with subgroups of suitable orders), and $T(G)=O(|G|^{3/4+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. Here $f(n)=\widetilde{\Theta}(g(n))$ means $f(n)=\Omega(g(n)(\log n)^a)$ and $f(n)=O(g(n)(\log n)^b)$ for some integers $a,b$, i.e. equality up to polylogarithmic factors. The conjecture asks for the true order of $T(n)$ and $T(G)$, between these bounds. This is additive combinatorics rather than graph theory.

title: Question 8
statement_text: Is the behavior of $T(n)$ different when $n$ is prime? How much does $T(G)$ depend on the structure of $G$ in addition to the order of $G$?
context_text: All groups are abelian. For subsets $W,C$ of a group $G$, $C$ is a complement for $W$ if $W+C=G$, and a minimal complement for $W$ if moreover no proper subset of $C$ is a complement for $W$; $C$ is a minimal complement in $G$ if it is a minimal complement for some $W\subseteq G$. For a finite abelian group $G$, $T(G)$ is the greatest $T$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at most $T$ is a minimal complement in $G$, and $T(n)$ is the minimum of $T(G)$ over abelian groups of order $n$. The authors prove $T(n)\ge\frac{n^{1/3}}{2(\log n/\log2)^{2/3}}$ (every non-empty $C$ with $|C|\le2^{2/3}n^{1/3}/(3e\log n)^{2/3}$ is a minimal complement), $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T(n)/\sqrt{n}\le\sqrt2$ (using groups with subgroups of suitable orders), and $T(G)=O(|G|^{3/4+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. The constructions of small subsets that are not minimal complements rely on the existence of subgroups of certain orders, so for $p$ prime (cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_p$, with no non-trivial subgroups) the best upper bound known is only $T(p)=O(p^{3/4+\varepsilon})$, while the authors conjecture $T(n)$ and $T(G)$ are $\sqrt{n}$, resp. $\sqrt{|G|}$, up to polylogarithmic factors. This is additive combinatorics rather than graph theory.

title: Question 9
statement_text: What is the optimal function $f$ such that every non-empty solid subset $C$ of a finite abelian group $G$ with $|C|\le f(|G|)$ is a maximal supplement in $G$?
context_text: $C$ is a supplement for $W$ if the translates $W+c$, $c\in C$, are pairwise disjoint, and a maximal supplement for $W$ if no proper superset of $C$ is a supplement for $W$; $C$ is a maximal supplement in $G$ if it is one for some $W$. A subset $C$ of $G$ is solid if it is not properly contained in any set $D$ with $D-D=C-C$; every maximal supplement must be solid, so small sets need not be maximal supplements but small solid sets are. The authors prove that there is an absolute constant $b>0$ such that every non-empty solid subset $C$ of a finite abelian group $G$ with $|C|\le b(|G|/\log|G|)^{1/4}$ is a maximal supplement in $G$, but it is unclear whether this bound is anywhere near optimal; they also show that in an infinite abelian group every finite non-empty solid subset is a maximal supplement. This is the dual of the analogous question for minimal complements ($W+C=G$ with $C$ minimal), where every non-empty subset of size $O(n^{1/3}/(\log n)^{2/3})$ of a group of order $n$ is a minimal complement. This is additive combinatorics rather than graph theory.

title: Question 10
statement_text: How does the probability that a random subset of a finite group $G$ with parameter $p = p(|G|)$ is a minimal complement (or maximal supplement) vary with $p$? Is there a (sharp) threshold?
context_text: All groups are abelian. For subsets $W,C$ of a group $G$, $C$ is a complement for $W$ if $W+C=G$, and a minimal complement for $W$ if moreover no proper subset of $C$ is a complement for $W$; $C$ is a minimal complement in $G$ if it is a minimal complement for some $W\subseteq G$. $C$ is a supplement for $W$ if the translates $W+c$, $c\in C$, are pairwise disjoint, and a maximal supplement for $W$ if no proper superset of $C$ is a supplement for $W$; $C$ is a maximal supplement in $G$ if it is one for some $W$. A random subset with parameter $p$ contains each element of $G$ independently with probability $p$. Being a minimal complement is not a monotone property, but the authors' results and proofs show that for small $p$ a random set is with high probability a minimal complement (every non-empty set of size at most about $|G|^{1/3}/(\log|G|)^{2/3}$ is one), and that for any $p>|G|^{\varepsilon-1/4}$ bounded away from $1$ (e.g. $p=1/2$) a random set is with high probability not a minimal complement. This is additive combinatorics rather than graph theory.
